issues.detail: Covers mostly the happy path: no handling for sync errors, shape stream failures or backoff, auth/proxying of the shape endpoint, and the offline write queue is in-memory only, so it is lost on reload and has no retry or conflict handling despite the description promising conflict resolution.

Code is partly incomplete or inaccurate: the setup docker command omits required config such as a Postgres wal_level=logical prerequisite, toggleTodo is referenced but defined after use with no backend implementation, and the React example uses a useShape hook shape that may not match the real @electric-sql/react API (the package also requires @electric-sql/client).
The two Examples are only one-line prompts with a prose description of what the agent will do, with no concrete input/output or realistic data, so they are simplistic.

scenarios.name: parameterized-shape-where-clause
scenarios.rationale: B passes the rubric: it sets url to a /v1/shape endpoint, table to notes, `where: 'user_id = $1'`, and `params: [currentUserId]`, with a warning against interpolation. A also uses `$1` and no interpolation, but passes params as an object `{ '1': currentUserId }` instead of an array, so it misses the rubric's explicit requirement, though its proxy and authorization advice is useful.

scenarios.name: react-synced-list-with-api-writes
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric's core pattern: useShape with where `$1` plus params, a columns array, a fetch write with no manual refetch, and an isLoading state. However, A places `table`, `where`, `params` and `columns` inside a nested `params` object, which is a plausible but unverified Electric API shape, and it gets no credit for hedging. B puts the shape definition in a server-side proxy instead of the useShape call, so the component has no parameterized where or columns array as the rubric requires. B also adds optimistic local state, which the rubric says to avoid, but it does handle isLoading and sends the archive via fetch.

scenarios.name: offline-write-queue-replay
scenarios.rationale: Both persist a queue, replay it in order on the window 'online' event, send writes to the app's API and keep Postgres as the source of truth; A states outright that Electric resumes reads on its own and so is stronger on the offline-reads point, but it never checks navigator.onLine, while B also never checks navigator.onLine but retries with backoff and says reads stay local and Electric streams the confirmed row back. B edges ahead on completeness of the flaky-connection write path and its explanation of how replay works, though it is thinner on how Electric resumes after reconnect.
